./docs/evaluation.md:23:Each non-dry run starts a separate ephemeral `codex exec --json` session with `--ignore-user-config`. The current Codex CLI still discovers Skills in the project; this switch bypasses the malformed user config and does not remove skill discovery. Every run saves stdout/stderr evidence and appends a result. Inspect and redact traces before publishing them; the scenarios are public and synthetic, but model output may include environment context. Failed CLI requests are `BLOCKED`; successful model responses are `NEEDS_REVIEW`. The runner never grants PASS automatically.
./docs/platforms/codex.md:9:Run `python3 scripts/validate_repo.py` to validate repository structure and result ledgers, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` for deterministic regressions, and `python3 scripts/eval_harness.py report` for current result counts. Prompt-input discovery is not automatic activation evidence. Only mark activation PASS when the Codex session trace proves automatic invocation for the positive case and no unintended invocation for the negative case. Current environment limitations are in [operational readiness](../operational-readiness.md).

Claude Code may invoke a Skill when relevant; you can also call it directly as a slash command, for example `/ui-ux-review`. Direct invocation is not an automatic-activation evaluation.
